title: Metrics / Logging System
subtitle: Designing a planet-scale observability platform (Datadog / Prometheus + Loki) with Gorilla XOR TSDB compression, inverted label indexes, and streaming alert evaluation
keyTakeaways: Prevent High-Cardinality Tag Explosion from crashing TSDB memory: decouple unique label combinations into a 64-bit `series_id` mapped via an Inverted Index (Roaring Bitmaps), and enforce per-tenant active time-series cardinality quotas at the ingestion edge.

Achieve 12x compression on time-series samples (16 bytes -> ~1.37 bytes/sample) using Facebook Gorilla encoding (Delta-of-Delta timestamps + XOR floating-point values) inside 2-hour immutable in-memory/disk blocks.

Store logs cost-effectively (Grafana Loki / ClickHouse pattern) by indexing only low-cardinality metadata labels (`service`, `env`, `region`, `level`) while streaming compressed log chunks (Zstd columnar blocks) directly to Object Storage (S3) with Bloom filters for fast full-text needle searches.

sections.heading: 1. Requirements Engineering & Scope Boundaries
sections.body: Modern cloud-native infrastructure requires a unified observability platform capable of ingesting tens of millions of metric data points and terabytes of structured application logs per second while powering real-time dashboards and sub-minute anomaly alerts.
bullets: Functional: Metrics Ingestion & Multi-Dimensional Tagging: Ingest counters, gauges, and histograms tagged with key-value labels (e.g., `http_requests_total{service="checkout", region="us-east", status="500"}`).

Functional: Structured Log Ingestion & Search: Ingest structured JSON logs and support filtering by label selectors (`{service="checkout", level="ERROR"}`) combined with full-text substring/regex search (`|= "NullPointerException"`).

Functional: PromQL / Time-Series Querying & Downsampling: Support range queries, aggregations (`sum by (region) (rate(.[5m]))`), and automatic historical rollups (raw 10s resolution for 15 days -> 1m resolution for 90 days -> 1h resolution for 2+ years).

Functional: Real-Time Alerting Engine: Continuously evaluate threshold and rate-of-change rules over sliding windows, deduplicate flapping alerts, and route notifications to PagerDuty, Slack, and webhooks.

Non-Functional: Write-Always Availability & Low Query Latency: 99.99% ingestion availability (observability must stay up when production is burning!); P99 dashboard query latency < 500ms for recent 6-hour windows; alert evaluation lag < 15 seconds.
Non-Functional: High Compression & Cost Efficiency: Eventual consistency of 2–5 seconds on ingestion visibility is acceptable in exchange for massive batching and 10x+ storage compression.
Out of Scope: Distributed request tracing span flamegraphs (Jaeger/Tempo UI) and Real User Monitoring (RUM) session replay video capture.

sections.heading: 2. Traffic Modeling & Workload Assumptions
sections.body: We size the platform for a large cloud enterprise monitoring 500,000 hosts and 10 Million ephemeral Kubernetes containers.
bullets: Monitored Fleet & Active Time Series: 10 Million containers emitting 50 distinct metrics each = 500 Million active time series (`series_id` combinations) collected every 10 seconds.
Log Volume per Day: 10 Million containers emitting an average of 20 log lines/sec = 200 Million log events/sec (~500 bytes raw JSON per log line).
Read:Write Ratio: Extremely write-heavy (~1,000:1 writes to dashboard/alert reads). Over 95% of ingested telemetry is never queried directly after the first 2 hours unless an incident occurs.
Peak Traffic Multiplier: 3x surge during cascading production outages (when error logs explode and hundreds of engineers open live dashboards simultaneously).

Payload Sizes: Raw metric sample = 16 bytes (8B `int64` timestamp + 8B `float64` value) -> compressed via Gorilla to **1.37 bytes/sample**; Raw log line = 500 bytes -> compressed via Zstd columnar chunking (8:1 ratio) to **~62.5 bytes/log**.

sections.heading: 3. Back-of-the-Envelope Capacity Calculations
sections.body: Without Gorilla time-series encoding and Zstd columnar log compression, storing 50 million metric samples/sec and 200 million log lines/sec for 5 years would bankrupt any organization.
bullets: Metrics Ingestion QPS: 500 Million active series / 10-second scrape interval = 50,000,000 samples/sec average -> 150,000,000 samples/sec at 3x peak (batched at 1,000 samples per gRPC OTLP request = 50,000 RPC/sec avg).
Log Ingestion QPS: 200,000,000 log lines/sec average (100 GB/sec raw uncompressed text -> 12.5 GB/sec on the wire with agent-side Zstd compression).

TSDB Head Block Memory (RAM): 500 Million active time series * (128 bytes series metadata/inverted index overhead + 2-hour Gorilla chunk buffer of 720 samples * 1.37 B = ~1,115 bytes per series) = ~557.5 GB total Head Block RAM across the TSDB Ingester fleet (e.g., 100 nodes * 16 GB RAM each, with RF=3 = 300 nodes).

5-Year Storage (Downsampled Metrics + Tiered Logs): Metrics raw (15-day retention) = 50M/s * 86,400s * 1.37 B = 5.92 TB/day (88.8 TB for 15d); 1-minute rollup (min/max/sum/count = 32B/min -> ~5.5B compressed/min) = 3.96 TB/day -> 5 years = 7.22 PB. Logs (30-day hot/warm S3 retention + 5-year compliance audit subset of 10% critical logs): 200M/s * 62.5 B = 12.5 GB/s = 1.08 PB/day compressed (32.4 PB for 30 days; 10% audit logs for 5 years = 108 TB/day * 1,825 = 197 PB S3 Glacier).
Network Bandwidth: Agent-compressed Ingress = ~68.5 MB/s (metrics) + 12.5 GB/s (logs) = ~12.57 GB/s (100.5 Gbps) across regional ingestion endpoints.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Samples per Series in 2 Hours (10s)    : 720 samples
Gorilla Compressed Chunk (720 * 1.37B) : ~986 bytes
In-Memory Series Label Map + Postings  : ~256 bytes / series
Total RAM per Active Series            : ~1,242 bytes
Total Cluster Head RAM (500M series)   : 500M * 1,242 B = 621 GB
With Replication Factor 3 (RF=3)       : 1.86 TB RAM across 120 Ingester Nodes

3. STORAGE (GORILLA TSDB + ZSTD COLUMNAR LOGS)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A) Metrics Storage:
   Raw 10s Resolution: 50M/s * 86,400s * 1.37 B = 5.92 TB/day (15d = 88.8 TB)
   1-Min Downsampled Rollups (5-Year Retention):
     500M series * 1,440 mins/day * 5.5 B (Gorilla rollup) = 3.96 TB/day
     5-Year Metrics S3 Storage = 3.96 TB * 365 * 5 = 7.23 PB

B) Logs Storage (500B raw -> 62.5B Zstd 8:1 compressed):
   Daily Compressed Log Volume: 200M/s * 86,400s * 62.5 B = 1,080 TB/day (1.08 PB)
   30-Day Standard Retention (S3 Standard) = 32.4 PB
   5-Year Security/Audit Retention (10% sampled critical logs in S3 Glacier):
     108 TB/day * 365 * 5 = 197.1 PB

================================================================================
4. NETWORK BANDWIDTH (WITH AGENT-SIDE ZSTD COMPRESSION)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Metrics Ingress (Compressed Batches)   : ~150 MB/s avg (450 MB/s peak)
Logs Ingress    (Zstd 8:1 on Agent)    : 12.5 GB/s avg (37.5 GB/s peak)
Query Egress    (Aggregated Series)    : ~400 MB/s
================================================================================

sections.heading: 4. API Interface Contracts & Data Domain Models
sections.body: Core external REST/gRPC/WebSocket API contracts, request/response payloads, and underlying storage entities with primary keys (PK), foreign keys (FK), secondary/clustering indexes (IDX), and relationship cardinalities.
bullets: POST /v1/metrics & POST /v1/logs (OTLP): Ingests batched, Zstd-compressed telemetry from OpenTelemetry DaemonSet agents.
GET /api/v1/query_range?query={promql}&start={t1}&end={t2}: Evaluates PromQL using Roaring Bitmap label intersection and Gorilla chunk decoding.
POST /api/v1/logs/search: Executes columnar log scan using Bloom Filter skip indexes before decompressing Zstd blocks.

sections.heading: 5. High-Level Architecture Blueprint & Component Topology
sections.body: The architecture follows the modern **Cortex / Thanos / Grafana Mimir & Loki** split: stateless Distributors validate and hash incoming batches; Ingesters buffer the latest 2 hours in a disk-backed Write-Ahead Log (WAL) and Gorilla memory chunks before flushing immutable blocks to S3; and Queriers federate real-time RAM state with historical S3 blocks.
bullets: DaemonSet Collector Agent (OTel / Vector): Runs on every host. Buffers telemetry in a local ring buffer, strips accidental PII/secrets via regex, pre-aggregates high-frequency counters over 10s windows, and compresses batches with Zstd.

Cardinality Guard & Distributor: Protects the cluster against a developer accidentally putting `user_id` or `request_id` into a metric label (which would spawn 100M+ useless series). Tracks active series per tenant using HyperLogLog / Redis sets and drops or strips offending labels when a tenant exceeds their quota.

TSDB Ingester (2-Hour Head Block + WAL): Appends samples to a local disk WAL for crash recovery and compresses them in memory using Gorilla XOR encoding. Every 2 hours, cuts an immutable block (Index + Chunks + Tombstones) and uploads it to S3.

Query Frontend & Federated Querier: Splits multi-day PromQL queries into 1-day sub-queries, checks a Redis step-aligned result cache, and fans out across Ingesters (for data `< 2h` old) and Store Gateways (for S3 blocks `> 2h` old).

sections.heading: 6. Deep-Dive Execution Flows & Core Logic
sections.body: We examine the two primary telemetry pipelines: Facebook Gorilla double-delta compression on ingestion and Roaring Bitmap inverted index queries on retrieval.
bullets: Gorilla Time-Series Compression (16 Bytes -> 1.37 Bytes / Sample): Telemetry agents collect metric samples every 10 seconds. Consecutive timestamps are compressed using Delta-of-Delta encoding (storing a single 0 bit when intervals are uniform), while consecutive floating-point values are XOR-encoded, reducing 16-byte `(timestamp, value)` pairs down to 1.37 bytes.

Inverted Index Roaring Bitmap Query Execution: When a query like `sum(rate(http_requests{status=500}))` arrives, the query engine retrieves posting lists for each label as compressed Roaring Bitmaps. The bitmaps are intersected using SIMD bitwise AND operations in CPU registers (<0.05 ms) to produce the exact set of matching time-series IDs, which are then read and decompressed from disk blocks.

sections.heading: 7. Production Hardening, Fault Tolerance & Resilience
sections.body: At planet scale, observability systems must defend against self-inflicted outages, query-of-death OOMs, and alert storms.
bullets: Automated Cardinality Linter & Adaptive Label Dropping: Continuously track the top-K highest-cardinality label keys per metric using Count-Min Sketch. If a deployment introduces a `session_id` label that spikes cardinality by 500,000 series in 60 seconds, automatically strip that single label key at the Distributor while preserving the rest of the metric.

Step-Aligned Query Result Caching & Query Splitting: A 30-day dashboard query (`now-30d` to `now`) spans 29 immutable historical days and 1 live day. The Query Frontend aligns timestamps to `step` boundaries, fetches the first 29 days directly from Redis query cache, and only evaluates the final live hours against the Ingesters.

Out-of-Order Sample Ingestion Window: Mobile and edge IoT agents occasionally buffer metrics offline and upload them 30 minutes late. Maintain a dedicated out-of-order WBL (Write-Behind Log) chunk in the TSDB Head that gets merged during the 2-hour block compaction.

Alertmanager Gossip Deduplication & Inhibition Rules: Run Alertmanager as a 3-node mesh using HashiCorp Memberlist gossip so all 3 replicas evaluate alerts independently without sending duplicate PagerDuty pages, and configure Inhibition Rules (e.g., if `ClusterNetworkDown` is firing, suppress 500 downstream `PodUnreachable` alerts).

Meta-Monitoring (Watching the Watcher): Deploy a tiny, isolated 'Canary Observability Cluster' in a separate cloud region that monitors the primary observability cluster's WAL disk space, Kafka consumer lag, and Alertmanager delivery health.

tradeOffs.option: Custom Gorilla TSDB + Label-Only Log Indexing (Mimir + Loki / ClickHouse)
tradeOffs.pros: 10–12x storage compression, immune to full-text index write amplification on logs, and seamless horizontal scaling backed by cheap S3 object storage.
tradeOffs.cons: Needle-in-a-haystack unindexed regex log searches across multi-TB windows require parallel brute-force chunk scanning (mitigated via Bloom filters and ClickHouse sparse primary indexes).
tradeOffs.bestFor: High-volume cloud infrastructure metrics and container logs where cost per TB and write throughput dominate.

tradeOffs.option: Full-Text Inverted Index for Everything (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch)
tradeOffs.pros: Sub-second arbitrary keyword and tokenized phrase search across every JSON field in logs.
tradeOffs.cons: Inverted index is often larger than the raw log data itself (1.2x–2x storage amplification), high JVM heap/GC pressure, and expensive shard rebalancing during traffic spikes.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Low-to-medium volume security SIEM logs or business audit events requiring ad-hoc full-text faceted search.

tradeOffs.option: Push vs. Pull (Prometheus Scrape) Ingestion Model
tradeOffs.pros: Pull lets the TSDB control scrape pacing and automatically detects target liveness (`up == 0`); Push works seamlessly across NAT gateways, serverless functions (AWS Lambda), and ephemeral short-lived jobs.
tradeOffs.cons: Pure Pull struggles across multi-VPC firewalls; pure Push requires edge rate-limiting and Distributor load balancers to prevent thundering herds.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Hybrid architecture: local host DaemonSet scrapes pods locally (Pull) and forwards compressed OTLP batches to the central regional Distributor (Push).

interviewTip: Interviewers love when you contrast **Metrics** vs. **Logs** storage internals: explain that Metrics use an **Inverted Index (`Label -> RoaringBitmap<SeriesId>`) + Gorilla XOR chunks** (where 16-byte samples shrink to `1.37 bytes`), whereas modern Logs (Loki/ClickHouse) avoid full-text indexing every word and instead index only low-cardinality labels + per-chunk **Bloom Filters** over Zstd-compressed columnar blocks on S3.
